correctness.rationale: Stand-alone exhaustive verification tests 1,048,576 vertex subsets with two distinct predicates, 62,048 nonempty simplices, an acyclic 31,000-pair matching and every one of 400,760 face-incidence arrows. The Morse model has one vertex, three 6-cells and forty-four 7-cells. Signed gradient elimination produces 44 integer differential columns, with a determinant -1 minor on masks 0x18e94, 0x55292, 0x61664. Since pi_6(wedge^3 S^6)=Z^3, these maps are classified by degrees and unimodular cancellation yields wedge^41 S^7. Independent mod-two ranks 6708, 9202, 7398, 2951, 509 verify the inferred Betti counts. The finite exhaustive check proves this finite graph result, not any graph family.

value.rationale: The Desargues graph is a canonical highly symmetric bipartite Kneser graph and Petersen double cover, with a previously classified ordinary independence complex. Allowing isolated induced edges defines the natural next filtration stage. Its nonpure 11-dimensional complex having exact integral homotopy of 41 seven-spheres is a substantive classification, not face counting or a generic model check, and provides a benchmark outside the chordal, cycle and tree cases. No downstream family theorem is claimed.
